react-router 6.30.3 is within the open-redirect advisory range (GHSA-2j2x-hqr9-3h42)
body:
## Description

`web/package.json` declares a caret range, and the lockfile resolves `react-router` / `react-router-dom` to **6.30.3**:

```json
// web/package.json:27
"react-router-dom": "^6.28.0",
```

```json
// web/package-lock.json:3570-3588
"node_modules/react-router":      { "version": "6.30.3", ... },
"node_modules/react-router-dom":  { "version": "6.30.3", ... },
```

Advisory **GHSA-2j2x-hqr9-3h42 / CVE-2026-40181** (open redirect via protocol-relative URL reinterpretation in `react-router`) affects `>= 6.7.0, < 6.30.4` and is fixed in **6.30.4**. The resolved 6.30.3 is inside that range. However, the advisory explicitly states it "only impacts applications **not** using Declarative Mode with `<BrowserRouter>`", and this app uses exactly declarative mode: `App.tsx:1` imports `BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Navigate` and renders `<BrowserRouter>` with `<Routes>`/`<Route>` — there is no `createBrowserRouter`/`RouterProvider` and no use of the vulnerable `redirect()` loader API anywhere in `web/src`. So the vulnerable code path is not reachable in current usage.

## Impact

No exploitable open redirect exists today because the project does not use the affected data-router `redirect` API. The risk is latent: the dependency version is within the advisory's affected range, so `npm audit` / SCA tooling will flag it, and any future migration to a data router (`createBrowserRouter` + loaders/actions using `redirect`) would expose the open-redirect path. Severity is **low** (downgraded from the suggested medium, and category corrected to supply-chain) and the original finding's premise that the version is "pinned at 6.28.0" is inaccurate — it resolves to 6.30.3 via the caret range.

## Required Fix

1. Bump to the patched line: update the lockfile so `react-router`/`react-router-dom` resolve to `>= 6.30.4` (e.g. `npm update react-router-dom`), clearing the advisory.
2. If/when migrating to a data router, validate all `redirect()` targets against an allowlist of internal paths and reject protocol-relative (`//host`) and absolute external URLs.

## References

- GHSA-2j2x-hqr9-3h42 / CVE-2026-40181 — react-router open redirect: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2j2x-hqr9-3h42
- CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect) — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html
- OWASP — Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards Cheat Sheet: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Unvalidated_Redirects_and_Forwards_Cheat_Sheet.html

Setup wizard accepts malformed Telegram api_hash (length-only check)
body:
## Description

The setup wizard's step-4 validation gates the Telegram credentials on a minimum length only:

```ts
// web/src/components/setup/SetupContext.tsx:130-134
case 4:
  // Telegram — phone required only for phone auth mode
  if (data.apiId <= 0 || data.apiHash.length < 10) return false;
  if (data.authMode === 'phone') return data.phone.startsWith('+');
  return true;
```

A Telegram `api_hash` is a fixed 32-character lowercase hexadecimal string. The check `data.apiHash.length < 10` accepts anything 10 characters or longer, so values of the wrong length (e.g. 11, 40) and values containing non-hex characters pass validation and advance the wizard.

## Impact

Malformed `api_hash` values are accepted by the UI and persisted/forwarded to the connect step, where they fail at the MTProto layer with an opaque downstream error instead of an actionable inline message at the point of entry. This is a low-severity input-validation/UX defect: it does not bypass a security control (the real check happens at connect time), but it lets clearly-invalid credentials through the wizard.

## Required Fix

1. Validate `api_hash` against its real format — `/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/i` — and `api_id` as a positive integer, surfacing an inline error when they do not match.
2. Keep the phone-format check; apply the format validation in the same step-4 branch so invalid credentials cannot advance.

## References

- CWE-20: Improper Input Validation — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html
